01

Brand Overview

Gwenda is a canalside ristobar at Schwartz Wharf, Hackney Wick, London — opening Summer 2026. It is not a restaurant with a drinks list. Not a bar with a kitchen annex. An archive salon where food, drink, art, and sound converge.

Craft cocktails, Italian small plates, natural wines, and vinyl on the decks — refined for candlelight and elevated for the lounge. The brand is deliberately, intentionally mysterious. Who is Gwenda? is a question, not an answer.

02

Logo

The Gwenda wordmark is the primary brand mark. It is always placed on a dark background — there is no light-background version. The wordmark is set in a refined serif typeface, reinforcing the archival and editorial character of the brand.

Approved usage

✓ Dark background — #0d0d0d

✓ Warm charcoal (print) — #23211b

Do not use

✗ Do not use

✗ Never on white or light backgrounds

Always use the logo at a generous size with clear space around it. Do not distort, recolour, or place on anything outside the brand dark palette.

Colour Palette

The palette is warm-dark and intentionally restrained. Every colour has a specific role. Do not introduce new colours.

Primary palette

Background #0d0d0d
Page body, hero, footer, all digital dark fills
Cream #e8e4dc
Body copy, headings, primary text
Gold #c9a84c
Accent — buttons, links, eyebrows, dividers
Muted #8a8680
Secondary copy, nav links, captions
Warm Charcoal #23211b
Print, Canva, business cards, flat off-screen fills

Extended palette (digital)

Elevated #141414
Base layer for story sections (before glow)
Card #1a1a1a
Email signup card
Gold Dark #8b6914
Depth / shadow in specific UI elements
Error #c97a7a
Form validation messages only

Print vs screen — the story section

The story section on the website is not a flat fill — it layers a dark base, a 4% gold glow, and 3.5% film grain. For print and Canva, always use the warm charcoal flat equivalent:

Story section — as seen on screen
Print / Canva equivalent

Warm Charcoal #23211b — use this for all flat print and off-screen design work. Do not use #141414 or #151414 for print — they are too dark and too cold.

Do not use

✗ Do not use white (#ffffff) as a background at any scale.
✗ Do not use #1c1b18 — this was an explicitly rejected charcoal substitute.
✗ Do not introduce bright or saturated colours — the palette is intentionally restrained.

04

Typography

Gwenda's identity is entirely serif. Do not use sans-serif typefaces in branded communications. The combination of Cormorant Garamond and Lora evokes print elegance — editorial, archival, unhurried.

Design Elements

Buttons

All buttons: uppercase, Cormorant Garamond 600, letter-spacing 0.08–0.1em, border-radius 2px. No pill shapes.

Enter our world Join the experience

Buttons on dark backgrounds — primary (gold fill) and ghost (transparent with gold border).

Enter our world Join the experience

Buttons shown on white for print reference — in use, always on dark backgrounds.

Dividers

1px gradient lines using gold at low opacity. Used beneath section headings, between blocks, and in menus.

What we serve

Film grain

A white noise texture at 3.5% opacity is applied site-wide. It adds tactility and an analogue feel — referencing print, archival materials, and late-night atmospheric spaces. Replicate in Canva by overlaying a grain texture at low opacity.

Behind the Doors
An archive salon

Canalside in Hackney Wick. The film grain overlay adds depth without distracting from the content — barely perceptible at 3.5% opacity, but unmistakably felt.

06

Voice & Tone

Gwenda's voice is evocative, restrained, and slightly mysterious. It is not corporate. It is not hard-sell. It is the voice of somewhere that knows exactly what it is and invites you to discover it yourself.

British English

Always write in British English. Dates in DD Month YYYY format (4 July 2026). Currency as £. Organise, not organize. Colour, not color.
